text:
sam-support: Customer reports GitHub OAuth flow failing after our LB change. They get an OAuth callback with `error=access_denied` and `error_description=state_mismatch` when signing in. Said it started ~yesterday after a proxy upgrade.
triage-bot: Ticket #5234 created by sam-support — https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/5234
jess-support: Can you paste the exact redirect_uri they registered and the raw callback URL they received?
sam-support: Registered redirect (on their GitHub OAuth app): `https://acme.example.com/auth/callback`
sam-support: Callback we see hitting their app: `https://acme.example.com:3000/auth/callback?code=...&state=abc+DEF/+/==` (raw from logs, state contains `+` and `/`)
alex-eng: That mismatch will fail GitHub's strict redirect_uri check — client must send exact redirect_uri used in the auth request. Two issues here: 1) the callback includes `:3000` while the registered URI has no port, 2) the PKCE/state uses base64 that contains `+` and `/` which may be mangled by some proxies if not URL-safe encoded.
alex-eng: Quick repro:
```
# simulate browser redirect generation
curl -v "https://github.com/login/oauth/authorize?client_id=XXX&redirect_uri=https://acme.example.com:3000/auth/callback&state=abc+DEF/+/=="
```
jess-support: Customer says they were not using :3000 before; our LB change added host normalization. Could be we changed how Host or forwarded-port is sent upstream.
mike-sre: I see a haproxy config deploy at 2026-03-16T19:03 that set `http-request set-header Host %[req.hdr(host),field(1,:)]` to normalize host. That will strip `:3000` from the Host header before sending to upstream. deploy-bot recorded change id `deploy-2026-0316-19`.
deploy-bot: deploy-2026-0316-19 completed — haproxy host-normalize. Rollback available.
alex-eng: So the app constructing the `redirect_uri` on the server side probably reads the downstream Host header or connection port — if Host lost port, it may still think it's running on :3000, generating a redirect with the port while the original request (and GitHub) expect no port. Also, when state uses standard base64, `+` can become space if any layer does form-decoding incorrectly — base64url avoids that.
alex-eng: Mitigations (ordered):
1) Short term for customer: register `https://acme.example.com:3000/auth/callback` as an allowed redirect on GitHub OR register `https://acme.example.com/auth/callback` and ensure your app generates that exact string.
2) We can patch the auth handler to prefer `X-Forwarded-Proto`/`X-Forwarded-Port` or the original `Host` header when constructing redirect_uri for OAuth checks.
3) Recommended: switch state/PKCE token encoding to base64url (RFC4648 §5) — replaces `+`/`/` with `-`/`_` and drops padding so it is safe in query strings.
alex-eng: I'll open a small PR to read `X-Forwarded-Port` and normalize redirect generation in the auth middleware; should be low-risk. If we want to revert the host-normalize deploy we can but that may reintroduce other issues.
sam-support: I'll pass the workaround (register portless + ported redirect) to the customer and ask if they can switch to base64url for state. Also asked if they want us to temporarily revert host-normalize.
jess-support: Marking ticket escalated to eng. @alex-eng can you link the PR here when ready? I'll update the customer with step-by-step repro we captured.
alex-eng: Will do. PR target branch: `hotfix/auth-redirect-normalize`. ETA 2-3 hours.
sam-support: Customer appreciates the quick triage. I'll keep them updated and confirm if the ported redirect registration fixes it.
jess-support: Thanks everyone — keeping this thread open until rollback/PR complete and customer confirms.
